items.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
items.summary: Officials have so far managed to avoid a repeat of last weekend's rioting and looting as hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations.

items.title: Watch: BBC in Paris as police charge protesters and use tear gas during unrest
items.summary: Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Paris where mostly peaceful protests turned into unrest after nightfall.

items.title: Storm Boelo amber warnings kick in as parts of UK brace for 80mph gusts
items.summary: Scotland, parts of northern England and Northern Ireland are forecast to be hit with the strongest winds from the country's second storm in as many days.

items.title: Ukraine depends on Starlink - can Europe plug the gap?
items.summary: Ukraine needs another satellite internet service, but a decent alternative to Elon Musk's network doesn't exist - yet.

items.title: Met Police says letter with claims about Meghan's father not shared with other law enforcement
items.summary: The Met said it passed information to the duchess but did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.

items.title: Voters in Brazil to choose between Lula and Bolsonaro's son
items.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil's jailed former president, is presenting a strong challenge to Lula, 80, who is seeking a fourth term in office.

items.title: Between quick wins and big dreams lies Burnham's biggest test
items.summary: The prime minister might be dreaming of gold medals in 2040, but he must first navigate the difficult years in between, writes Laura Kuenssberg.

items.title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm
items.summary: Scotland editor James Cook finds out what life is like on board a ship in an untapped oil field awaiting its fate.
